histories.MatterHistoryActionText: The resolution was recommended for a two-meeting deferral by the Rules, Confirmations, and Public Elections Committee. Council Member Cortese moved that the Resolution be deferred to the November 5, 2026 Council meeting, which motion was seconded and approved by a voice vote of the Council.

The resolution was approved with a substitute by the Rules, Confirmations, and Public Elections Committee. Council Member Cortese moved that the resolution be adopted, which motion was properly seconded. Council Member Cortese offered a substitute resolution and moved that it be adopted, which motion was seconded and approved by a voice vote of the Council.
Council Member Cortese moved that the Resolution be adopted, which motion was seconded and approved by the following roll call vote:

text:
..title
A resolution requesting the Metropolitan Nashville Airport Authority to collaborate with the Federal Aviation Administration in consideration of residents affected by changes to air traffic patterns at Nashville International Airport.
..body
WHEREAS, the Federal Aviation Administration (“FAA”) began testing new flight paths in 2024, residents of southern Davidson County, including Nipper’s Corner, Bradford Hills, Oak Hill, Crieve Hall, Whispering Hills, and Forest Hills, noticed an increased number of flights over their residences; and
WHEREAS, concerned residents notified the FAA of their complaints throughout the testing period. Despite these complaints, the new flight paths were finalized in 2025; and
WHEREAS, residents in portions of southern Davidson County have reported substantial increases in aircraft activity over their neighborhoods following implementation of the new departure headings and have raised concerns regarding aircraft noise and its impact on their quality of life; and
WHEREAS, residents now continue to experience increased air traffic, noting over 150 flights a day over some residences. This increased air traffic is counter to FAA’s stated goals of the project to disperse air traffic both vertically and horizontally; and
WHEREAS, residents have reported noise levels of up to 90 dB at ground level due to flights overhead; and
WHEREAS, according to the United States Environmental Protection Agency, noise pollution can lead to high blood pressure, hearing loss, sleep disruption, and lost productivity; and
WHEREAS, Radnor Lake is a Class II State Natural Area known to be a haven for wildlife, particularly migrating birds and worthy of perpetual preservation; and
WHEREAS, residents have expressed concern regarding the impact of increased air traffic on Radnor Lake and surrounding communities and have expressed dissatisfaction with the level of community engagement preceding implementation of the new departure headings that the FAA has failed to consider the impact that increased air traffic would have on Radnor Lake and surrounding and did not properly engage affected communities ahead of making the proposed changes; and 
WHEREAS, residents have requested that their concerns regarding aircraft noise and increased aircraft activity be documented and communicated to the appropriate federal authorities, and that reliable information regarding aircraft activity and noise impacts be made available to affected communities methods to decrease disruption from overhead flights including rebalancing departures or and supporting higher climb profiles over residential areas where possible. Further, residents have requested efforts to better inform the public including noise-monitoring review in affected areas; and
WHEREAS, flight paths and departure headings are established and regulated by the Federal Aviation Administration, and neither the Metropolitan Government nor the Metropolitan Nashville Airport Authority has authority to independently establish or alter those headings; and
WHEREAS, the FAA has communicated to state and local elected officials that the departure headings implemented in 2025 are final, while acknowledging that FAA procedures may be subject to future review or modification under applicable federal processes; and
WHEREAS, it is fitting and proper that the Metropolitan Council support community groups in the pursuit to protect the public health and safety of Nashvillians and our wildlife areas.
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE COUNCIL OF THE METROPOLITAN GOVERNMENT OF NASHVILLE AND DAVIDSON COUNTY: 
Section 1. That the Metropolitan Council hereby goes on record as requesting that the Board of Commissioners of the Metropolitan Nashville Airport Authority continue to provide the Federal Aviation Administration with information regarding concerns reported by residents affected by aircraft operations; make available to the public relevant and reliable information regarding aircraft activity and noise impacts to the extent such information is available; communicate to affected residents any future FAA proposals or proceedings involving material changes to departure procedures at Nashville International Airport; and continue to coordinate with the FAA regarding documented community concerns, available aircraft activity and noise information, and any future FAA review of departure procedures. collaborate with the Federal Aviation Administration to review the effects of flight patterns on affected neighborhoods and continue to inform citizens of any updates. 
Section 2. That the Metropolitan Clerk is directed to transmit a copy of this resolution to the Metropolitan Nashville Airport Authority Board Chair Nancy Sullivan and the Board of Commissioners of the MNAA. 
Section 3. That this resolution shall take effect immediately upon its adoption, the welfare of the Metropolitan Government of Nashville and Davidson County requiring it.
